newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Febec officials back change in coffee body.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Febec officials back change in coffee body.

text.p: Officials of Brazil's Coffee Exporters' Federation (Febec) have in principle given their backing to a plan outlining a change in the federation's statutes, Febec's president said.

"In principle, the plan, with very few details to be changed, was approved. It now has to be submitted to a general assembly," said Oswaldo Aranha after a meeting of Febec officials in Vitoria, Espirito Santo state.
No date had so far been set for the assembly, he added.

One of the main changes is a system in which council seats would be decided according to the number of bags shipped by each regional center, with associations then nominating their own representatives.
Each association's exports would not be determined by the amount shipped from ports in the region but by total shipments by its members.
Therefore, exports by the Vitoria association, for example would include all coffee shipped by members out of any port in Brazil and not just Vitoria.
Likewise coffee shipped out of Vitoria by a company which belonged to the Rio de Janeiro association would not be counted in Vitoria's exports.
Currently the council is comprised of 35 companies which are agreed by consensus. The companies then nominate their representatives to sit on the council.
The change will mean the Febec is more of a federation, dealing with the regional associations and not directly with individual countries.
This however is not expected to meet with the support of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Association (Abecafe), formed as a break-away group in November 1995.

Recently talks have been held to see if there is any way to unite the two groups in a new entity but one of Abecafe's goals is that any new body should be made up of individual companies and not regional associations.
"Abecafe has to understand what we did and that it is absolutely fair," Aranha said.
